I find an analogy helps me understand the ontological argument better:

Consider the statement S1= "There is no objective truth." (I am not super precise with the term 'objective' here, forgive me, but this is just a quick analogy after-all.)

Okay, well, isn't S1 an objective truth itself? If S1 is true then S1 is an example of an objective truth and therefore objective truth exists. This is a contradiction, therefore S1 is false. Then its contrary "There is AN objective truth" is true. (I'm sorry if this is written out too simplistically, I just want to make the point clear.)

Therefore, by its sheer definition (or better: inherently in the concept), objective truth must exist.

The ontological argument make a similar case for **'The First Cause' **or 'Logos' or whatever we should call the Existence Itself. We Christians like to identify it with the Judeo-Christian God, which is matter of faith but also based on historical evidence.

To get a better idea of what classical philosophers mean by Existence Itself consider Nothing as mentioned in the comic. Be sure to consider the real Nothing, for example even complete vacuum has particles coming in/out of existence - it's not Nothing. No thing and no body exists within Nothing and no thing can start existing ortherwise it would not be Nothing, but 'That-Quasi-Nothing-That-Actually-Spawned-Something'. As an alternative to our existing universe there could just have 'been' Nothing. Existence Itself is somewhat the opposite of Nothing - it must exist by its sheer definition.

First, I define the term 'contingent' - I'm sorry for yet another word, but it's a very useful handle on a concept here. Some thing is contingent if it depends on some other thing for its existence. For example, I depend on the existence of my atoms to exist myself. In fact, everything that has the possibility of not existing is contingent - something else is making it exist at the time and place it does exists.

Okay, now suppose everything that exists is contingent then there is no reason why instead of the Nothing we have the universe. (Since everything is waiting for something else to make it exist.) But we exist along with the rest of the visible universe, so there is some thing that by its sheer definition must exist - it doesn't have an option of not existing. That thing is Existence Itself. (In fact, it can be argued that there is only one such thing and it has no parts, but I don't want to get into that.)
